# List of U.S. states and territories by population
## Electoral apportionment
### House of Representatives
[edit]
Based on this decennial census, each state is allocated a portion of the 435 fixed seats in the United States House of Representatives (until the early 20th century, the apportionment process generally increased the size of the House based on the results of the census until the size of the House was capped by the Reapportionment Act of 1929), with each state guaranteed at least one Representative. The allocation is based on each state's proportion of the combined population of the fifty states (not including the District of Columbia, Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, or the U.S. Virgin Islands).

# List of U.S. states and territories by population
## Electoral apportionment
### Electoral College
[edit]
The Electoral College, every four years, elects the President and Vice President of the United States based on the popular vote in each state and the District of Columbia. Each state's number of votes in the Electoral College is equal to its number of members in the Senate plus members in the House of Representatives.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-auto-5)
The Twenty-third Amendment to the United States Constitution additionally grants the District of Columbia (D.C.), which is not a state, as many Electoral College votes as it would have if it _were_ a state, while having no more votes than the least populous state (Wyoming). Since the U.S. Constitution guarantees every state at least one member of the U.S. House of Representatives and two members of the U.S. Senate, every state has at least three Electoral College votes. Thus, the Electoral College has 538 members (100 senators, plus 435 representatives due to the limit imposed by the Reapportionment Act of 1929, plus 3 members for the District of Columbia).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-auto-5)Territories of the United States are not included in the Electoral College: people in those territories cannot vote directly for the President of the United States,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-6) although they may participate in the partisan nominating primaries and caucuses.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-7)

Thus, the Electoral College has 538 members (100 senators, plus 435 representatives due to the limit imposed by the Reapportionment Act of 1929, plus 3 members for the District of Columbia).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-auto-5)Territories of the United States are not included in the Electoral College: people in those territories cannot vote directly for the President of the United States,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-6) although they may participate in the partisan nominating primaries and caucuses.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-7)

**States that meet all three conditions**

| State | Population rank 2020 | Biden % – Trump % 2020 (margin) | Teen birth rate 2020 (per 1,000 females 15‑19) | Suicide mortality rate 2020 (per 100 000 total pop) | Qualifies? |
|-------|-----------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| California | 1 | ~ +29 % (63.5 % vs 34.3 %) | **11.0** | **9.55** | **Yes** |
| New Jersey | 11 | ~ +20 % (59.3 % vs 39.2 %) | **9.2** | **6.65** | **Yes** |
| Massachusetts | 16 | ~ +33 % (65.6 % vs 32.1 %) | **6.1** | **8.26** | **Yes** |

### How the conditions were verified  

| Criterion | Data source | Why it meets the threshold |
|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|
| *20 most populated states in 2020* | U.S. Census 2020 population table (top 20 list) | The states listed above are all in the top‑20 (CA 1st, TX 2nd, …, CO 20th). |
| *Biden winning by ≥10 % margin* | 2020 U.S. Presidential Election results (state‑level percentages) | California: 63.48 % vs 34.32 % (Δ ≈ 29 %); New Jersey: 59.26 % vs 39.19 % (Δ ≈ 20 %); Massachusetts: 65.60 % vs 32.14 % (Δ ≈ 33 %). |
| *Teen birth rate ≤13 per 1,000 females 15‑19* | CDC “Teen Births” (2020) table | California: 11.0; New Jersey: 9.2; Massachusetts: 6.1. All are ≤ 13. |
| *Suicide mortality rate ≤11 per 100 000* | CDC “Suicide Mortality” (2020), age‑adjusted rate | California: 9.55; New Jersey: 6.65; Massachusetts: 8.26. All are ≤ 11. |

Thus **California, New Jersey, and Massachusetts** are the only U.S. states in the top 20 by 2020 population that simultaneously:  
1. Had a Democratic presidential win with a margin of **≥10 %**,  
2. Had a teen birth rate of **≤13 per 1,000 females aged 15‑19**, and  
3. Had a suicide mortality rate of **≤11 per 100,000 total population** in 2020.
